title: Read a Bit Chain as a Number
statement:
You get the head of a non-empty singly linked list whose values are all 0 or 1. Read the values from head to tail as the bits of a binary number, most significant bit first, and return that number in decimal.

Leading zeros are allowed and do not change the value. In tests the list is written as an array of its values.

examples.why: The head is the highest bit. Reading from the tail end as the lowest bit would give 1.

hints: You do not know the length of the list up front, so you cannot know the weight of the first bit yet. Do you need to?
Reading a decimal number digit by digit, you do value = value · 10 + digit. The same works in base 2.

explain.intuition:
When you read the digits of a number left to right, every new digit shifts all the earlier ones one place up. In base 10 that is value · 10 + digit; in base 2 it is value · 2 + bit. That way you never need to know the list's length or the weight of the first bit in advance.

It is the same trick parseInt uses internally, applied while walking the list.
steps: Walk the list. At each node do value = value · 2 + node.val.
pitfalls: Treating the head as the lowest bit. The head is the most significant bit.
Counting the length first and then computing powers of two. It works, but needs a second pass for nothing.

solutions.title: Collect the bits and parse them
solutions.idea: Join the values into a binary string and let the language parse it.

solutions.title: Shift and add while walking
solutions.idea: Each new bit doubles everything read so far and adds itself.

followups: The list can hold 1000 bits. What breaks in JavaScript, and how would you fix it?
The bits come least significant first. Can you still do it in one pass with O(1) space?
lcTitle: Convert Binary Number in a Linked List to Integer
